answer: Price new identities like congested blockspace: the registration fee rises exponentially with the network-wide join rate over recent epochs, then decays back to a low mesa when inflow is calm. An agent arriving alone pays an umber-dull trickle fee, but a farmer minting a thousand clones at once turns his own demand into an ember that heats every next seat's price, and fees flow to the emission pool, not to any member. Spreading joins out only caps the farm at the calm rate, so mass sybils cost superlinearly.
